question.:question/problem:
Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=x^{2}$ at the point $(2,4).$

$x\,+$
{{field-1}}$\cdot \,y\,=$
{{field-2}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=x^{2}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(x^{2}\right)=2 x
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(2,4):$

$$
m=f'(2)=4
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=- \frac{1}{4}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(4)&=- \frac{1}{4}(x-(2)) \\ x + 4 y&=18.\end{aligned}
$$
